concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. High fidelity art direction concept for the playable satirical card strategy game PARANOID TIMES. Original cohesive British 1990s red-top tabloid newspaper art direction, a humorous news-of-the-world parody with conspiracies, not a reproduction of any real newspaper logo. Looks like an expensive finished indie card game. Warm off-white newsprint #EFE6D2, near-black ink #181817, rich crimson #B51D25, tiny restrained teal ownership accents and mustard marks. Large perfectly legible heavy condensed newspaper headlines; elegant readable serif story copy; monospaced small metadata. A bold red masthead with exact white title PARANOID TIMES. Grainy black-and-white candid press photos with halftone; photographic absurdity in otherwise mundane scenes. Authentic subtle paper fibers, fine print rules, cutout captions, occasional crooked rubber stamps. Visual hierarchy must be calm enough to play: texture is secondary, actions have clear contrast and generous touch targets. Flat front-facing digital interface, no physical device, no angled presentation, no external props, no collage of several screens, no generic neon sci-fi HUD, no gradients, no glowing fantasy jewels, no tiny unreadable status. One complete single screen per image. These are design concepts, not evidence of working software.
Create one landscape 16:9 PC battle screen. At top PARANOID TIMES masthead, issue NO. 07, YOUR TURN, small accessible speaker control reading MUSIC ON. Strong newspaper composition with wide central map article and two clean narrow side columns; no sprawling dashboard. Top status strip: TRUTH 54%, YOUR IP 12, RIVAL IP 9, 2 PLAYS LEFT.
Center US map on printed newsprint, accurate general continental silhouette with boundaries, small teal and crimson state tints, clearly highlighted Texas with ink circle. Center section heading THE BATTLE FOR THE FRONT PAGE. A small black-and-white press photograph tucked in the right column shows a moth-like cryptid solemnly approaching a microphone. Left column "EDITOR'S DESK", concise objectives; right "LATEST DISPATCH", recent action.
Bottom hand area has FIVE beautiful separate cards, full readable titles, consistent ivory frames and large cost circles. 1: Blurry Bigfoot Photo Goes Viral, cost3, MEDIA, Truth +1, amateur cryptid photo. 2: UFO Over High School Football Game, cost5, ZONE, Pressure +2, saucer over floodlit school stadium. 3: Mothman Public Warning, cost3, ATTACK, Rival IP -2. 4: Elvis the UFO Pilot, cost5, MEDIA, Truth +3, Elvis in pilot cockpit. 5: Tinfoil Hat Distribution Drive, cost2, ATTACK, Rival IP -1. Use game-card art printed in grayscale, keep cards organized and reachable. Right bottom large crimson GO TO PRESS button, separate from cards. The game must feel like editing a mischievous front page, with the actual map and card choices occupying most screen area. UI strings in English.

Create one portrait 3:4 between-round newspaper reading screen. Mostly a gorgeous full front page of PARANOID TIMES, authentic red-top layout. Top issue line "ROUND 7 • LATE EDITION". Huge black condensed main headline exactly "BIGFOOT HIRES MOTHMAN AS PRESS SECRETARY". Smaller subheadline "UFO stadium flyover turns a local warning into a national briefing." Byline "By the Paranoid Times Night Desk".
Small side story box "OFFICIAL RESPONSE" with deadpan text "No anomalies detected." and a redacted paragraph. A small row labelled "THE CARDS BEHIND THE STORY" displays exactly three tiny source cards: "Blurry Bigfoot Photo Goes Viral", "Mothman Public Warning", "UFO Over High School Football Game". This illustrates a new coherent story built from those cards, not three unrelated copied headlines. Footer outside the page has page navigation and one large red "CONTINUE TO ROUND 8" button. Keep newspaper highly legible and entertaining. Do not invent numerical gameplay rewards in this newspaper concept.

Create one landscape 16:9 in-game BREAKING news popup design, captured mid-reveal. Underlying printed map and card hand remain clearly recognizable around the popup, only lightly dimmed, never a black screen. Center a bold editorial extra-edition clipping occupying about half the screen width, ivory torn-edge paper with restrained crimson outline, header "BREAKING", massive headline "THE BALLOON HAS A PILOT". Large grainy black-and-white amateur photo of a clearly saucer-shaped craft with an Elvis-like pilot smiling out of the window above a floodlit field. Do not add a full-screen explosion, a giant opaque black backdrop, or duplicate overlapping popups. Gorgeous, witty, highly polished and readable.

ONLY replace the small TODAY'S OBJECTIVES block in the left column with an accurate Truth faction win-condition panel. Title: 'TRUTH SEEKERS'. Three clear alternative objectives with empty square indicators: 'Reach 90% Truth', 'OR control 10 states', 'OR build 200 IP'. Delete the old incorrect 'Keep Truth above 40%' and old checklist items. Keep all other content unchanged. This is a concept screen, not a new rule system.

Edit this PARANOID TIMES newspaper concept.
